title: Standby integrity prober and tier-routing validator for multi-region cutovers
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic readiness prober that evaluates warm standby instances before region cutover and validates tier-aware routing tables and fallback model variant compatibility. The prober should produce a single readiness score (0-100) and a short diagnostic payload that can gate automated region failover, trigger runbook steps, or mark candidates as ineligible for promotion.

Background: Current warm-standby activation is based on coarse health checks and cache fill heuristics. We've observed two classes of failures during DR switches: (1) cold KV caches leading to large latency spikes and model OOMs due to incompatible quantization kernels, and (2) misrouted traffic where tier routing rules point to capacity-constrained pools. This ticket defines probes across the stack that can be run continuously and on-demand prior to cutover to assert readiness and provide actionable diagnostics.
tasks: Design probe spec: KV prefix coverage, model variant smoke queries, tier routing table sanity checks
Implement prober binary (go) with pluggable checks and scoring weights
Add non-invasive prefix-warming flow that respects burst throttles and cache TTLs
Model variant compatibility test harness (small input set; verify output shape, tokens, kernel errors)
Tier routing validator: verify pool capacities, queue depth thresholds, and fallback mappings
Integrate readiness score into regional failover controller as a gating signal
Expose probe results and history in Console (new dashboard panel and alerting thresholds)
E2E test: simulate cutover with primed vs unprimed fleets, measure 95th latency and error rates
Write runbook steps and automated remediation actions (eviction avoidance, prefetch ramp)
acceptance_criteria: Readiness prober produces a reproducible score and diagnostics within 30s for a typical fleet
Controller rejects automated cutover if candidate region readiness_score < 75
Prefetch warming does not exceed configured burst allowance and respects tenant isolation
Model variant compatibility check detects binary/kernel mismatches and surfaces clear remediation
New Console panel shows last 48h readiness trends for every region and tier
E2E simulated cutover with readiness gating reduces 95th-percentile failover latency by >= 40% compared to baseline
metrics: prefetch_coverage: percent of hot prefixes available in KV cache pre-cutover (target >= 60%)
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag prober as read-only and ship to staging. 2) Collect telemetry for two weeks to calibrate scoring weights per tier. 3) Enable gating in canary region for low-traffic customers and run simulated cutovers nightly. 4) Gradually enable automated gating for all non-critical regions. 5) Document emergency disable path and include manual override in runbook.
risks_and_mitigation: Aggressive prefetch could overload GPUs or network: mitigate with token-bucket burst limit and tenant-aware quotas
False negatives due to transient network glitches: run three probes spaced 10s apart and use median for gating
Model variant false positives (passing smoke tests but failing under load): include a randomized load-smoke that validates KV/attention memory pressure at small scale
Operator confusion on score interpretation: include human-readable diagnostics and recommended remediation actions in Console
test_plan: Unit tests for each probe type (KV, model-variant, routing) with mocked backends
Integration tests that run prober against a replica staging fleet and verify diagnostic payloads
Chaos scenario: drop a fraction of KV nodes and confirm readiness_score drops and controller blocks cutover
Load test: run prober across all regions and ensure it completes within SLAs and stays under burst limits
